title: Pinned comparison of lattice and sectionwise regular derived cups
statement: Let $R$ be any commutative condensed ring and let $r\geq0$. Use the ordinary action category $\operatorname{Action}(\operatorname{Mod}_R,\mathbf Z^r)$, its invariant limit and its derived functor in localization universe $u+2$ from [lem-sfb-discrete-lattice-koszul-resolution]. Use also the sectionwise condensed action category for the discrete group $\operatorname{ULift}(\mathbf Z^r)$ and its normalized derived invariants and regular-coefficient cup in localization universe $u+1$ from [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-restriction-calculus]. Define a bridge datum as an exact additive equivalence from sectionwise actions to ordinary actions, an underlying-module isomorphism intertwining every constant group section, and an invariant-functor isomorphism whose composite with the sectionwise invariant inclusion is the ordinary invariant inclusion followed by the underlying-module isomorphism. The coefficient universe transport is the functor on derived categories induced by the identical exact functor on internal modules. The derived bridge is a natural isomorphism from the derived action equivalence followed by ordinary derived invariants to sectionwise derived invariants followed by this coefficient transport, normalized on EVERY complex by the two computation units, the localized invariant comparison, and the canonical localization factorization maps. The regular-coefficient identification is the localization of the underlying-module identification with the regular trivial action algebra. Give coefficient universe transport the strong tensor structure fixed by the flat-term K-flat representative equation and localized ordinary unit of [def-sfb-lattice-derived-invariants-tensor]. Define compatibility to mean that the resulting regular-coefficient derived invariants isomorphism carries both the binary cup and cup unit of the restriction calculus to the binary cup and unit of [def-sfb-lattice-algebra-derived-cup], using that tensorator and the localized regular-unit identification. This defines the datum and predicate; existence and compatibility are conclusions of the consuming theorem.
